title: CraveControl - Usage of Biofeedback in the reduction of craving in alcohol addiction
summary: The study examines whether biofeedback is an appropriate intervention to reduce addictive pressure/strong desire for alcohol in people with existing alcohol dependence. This is examined by comparing two groups, one receiving normal inpatient therapy and the second group receives additional biofeedback interventions. The latter involves a diagnostic phase, a training phase and a transfer phase where the test subjects are confronted with the addictive substance. At the beginning, after the training and transfer phase, measurements and questionnaires are carried out, and the questionnaires are sent out again one month after the end of the intervention.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of alcohol: Dependence syndrome
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of alcohol dependence according to ICD-10
Completed withdrawal
at least 3 days of abstinence before inclusion in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Withdrawal symptoms during clinical examination
Further substance dependence (exception: nicotine)
Very strong nicotine dependence (FTNA greater than or equal to 7)
Acute suicidality
Contraindication biofeedback: epilepsy, severe personality disorder, Botox in the frontalis muscle in the last 3 months, psychosis)
Limited language skills
Hyperhidrosis
Skin diseases (dermatitis, psoriasis, severe acne, burns where electrodes are applied, skin infections, allergic reactions, severe pruritus)
Accommodation according to PsychKG
Lack of ability to consent
Patients who are not suitable according to the recruiter's discretion (lack of adherence, no motivation to abstinence, heart disease, pacemaker)
